content.title: About
content.content: Raw fig is a sweet, juicy fruit of the fig tree (Ficus carica) native to the Mediterranean, parts of Asia, and the United States. The fruit has a soft flesh covered by a thin edible skin and contains tiny edible seeds. Figs are eaten fresh and also used in desserts, salads, and preserves.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Fig belongs to the mulberry family and is one of the oldest cultivated fruits, grown for over 5,000 years.
The edible fruit develops from an inverted flower inside a structure called a syconium, not from external blossoms.
There are more than 200 fig varieties, differing in flesh color, flavor, and size.
In ancient Egypt, Greece, and Rome, figs were called the “fruit of the gods.”
Fig seeds are rich in fiber and healthy fats.

items.title: Rich in dietary fiber
items.content: Figs provide both soluble and insoluble fiber, supporting healthy digestion and blood sugar regulation.

items.title: Source of vitamin K
items.content: Raw figs contain vitamin K, which is important for blood clotting and bone health.

items.title: Contains antioxidants
items.content: Flavonoids and polyphenols in figs help protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Supports heart health
items.content: Potassium and magnesium in figs contribute to normal blood pressure and heart function.

items.title: Provides essential minerals
items.content: Figs are a good source of calcium, iron, and magnesium, needed for bones and blood formation.

items.title: Allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience an allergic reaction to figs, especially if they are allergic to other mulberry family plants.

items.title: High sugar content
items.content: Fresh figs contain a notable amount of natural sugars, so people with diabetes should monitor portion sizes.

items.title: Digestive issues
items.content: Large amounts of figs can cause gas and discomfort due to their high fiber content.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Raw figs can be eaten as a snack, added to salads, yogurts, oatmeal, and used in baking, jams, and sauces. Before eating, rinse the fruit and optionally peel the skin.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store figs in the refrigerator in an airtight container for up to 5–7 days. For longer storage, freeze the fruit after removing the skin.
